html:
A famine along the Volga and in the Urals in 1921 and 1922 that killed around five million people.

It came at the end of the Russian Civil War. To feed the Red Army and the cities, the Bolsheviks had seized grain from peasants by force. Peasants answered by sowing less, and many revolted. Then came a severe drought in 1921, and the harvest failed across a vast area. People ate grass, bark and clay, and there were reports of cannibalism. Disease followed hunger.

Lenin's government, already shifting to the New Economic Policy, which let peasants sell their surplus, had to accept foreign aid. The American Relief Administration, led by Herbert Hoover, fed around ten million people a day at its peak, and the Norwegian explorer Fridtjof Nansen led other relief. The state also used the famine as a reason to seize church treasures.

A famine struck the Kazakh steppe at the same time, the Kazakh famine of 1919 to 1922. Worse ones followed under Stalin, including the Holodomor.
sum: A famine along the Volga and in the Urals in 1921 and 1922 that killed around five million people.
